title: The molecular basis of ADP-ribose pyrophosphorylation by a phage PRPS-like enzyme in NAD+ reconstitution.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and read the full 9-page supplementary PDF (the only supplementary file): 9 figure legends plus 2 tables, both of which are crystallography/cryo-EM collection statistics, not biological measurements. Queried the Protein Data Bank (PDB, the public archive of 3D protein structures) for all three deposited entries (23BM, 27FN, 23CA): all return HTTP 404 (not released); a control entry (7XMU) returns 200, so the query works. Queried the Electron Microscopy Data Bank (EMDB) for both maps: EMD-81126 has status HPUB (hold until publication) and EMD-68853 has status AUTH (hold until author release), with author names listed as SUPPRESSED.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The enzyme kinetics (Michaelis constant Km and turnover number kcat for wild-type Adps and four alanine variants, three replicates each), the LC-MS (liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry) product assay, the magnesium dependence, and the alignment of Adps homologs are described only in figure legends. I could not check their underlying numeric values because no numeric table or sequence file was deposited anywhere.

a1_downloadable.note: All five deposited datasets are still embargoed despite the paper being published. The three PDB structure entries return 404 at the RCSB data API, EMD-81126 is on 'hold until publication' and EMD-68853 is on 'hold until author release'. Nothing can be downloaded today.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No label column exists anywhere. The only quantitative biology (Km, kcat, percent activity) lives inside figure panel images in the supplementary PDF and would have to be read off graphs by hand.

a3_inputs_present.note: The multiple sequence alignment of Adps homologs (Supplementary Fig. S4) is an image only; no FASTA file of the aligned sequences was deposited, so the sequence inputs are a picture, not data.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated clearly in the figure legends and statistics tables (angstroms, electrons per square angstrom, millimolar MgCl2), but there is no data file for them to apply to.

a5_enough_rows.note: Three structures of a single protein (one X-ray at 2.61 angstrom, two cryo-EM at 2.76 and 2.98 angstrom), five enzyme variants measured (wild type plus His121Ala, Asp161Ala, Asp212Ala, Asp213Ala) and one extra variant tested qualitatively (Lys185Ala). That is roughly ten kinetic numbers total, against a checklist minimum of about 1,500 labelled rows.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~3 MB supplement; structure files would be a few MB if released
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small, but there is nothing to fit.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The supplementary statistics tables are internally consistent with the paper's claims (282 modelled residues, 82,500 and 66,000 final particles), but with no released data there is nothing independent to cross-check.

a8_label_provenance.note: The measurements that do exist are genuine physical ones (synchrotron diffraction, cryo-EM, LC-MS, steady-state kinetics), not another model's output; AlphaFold3 was used only as a molecular replacement search model, not as a source of labels.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) would be the obvious choice for phage anti-defence proteins, but there is no labelled data here to fit a head on

integration.partner_dataset: None usable. The one identifier present (UniProt accession F1D1Q1, the Adps protein) is a single protein, so any 'join' would be a lookup of one row.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: one protein joins to one row in any partner resource, which is a database query, not a dataset.

controls.positive_control: None possible; no model can be trained.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: this is a three-structure mechanistic enzymology paper on a single phage enzyme, with about ten kinetic measurements reported as figure panels and no released coordinates.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use phage protein sequence to predict whether an enzyme rebuilds the cell's energy-carrier molecule NAD+ during infection.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would show a model a phage protein sequence and ask whether it belongs to the NAD+-rebuilding pathway. This paper supplies exactly one such sequence (UniProt F1D1Q1) plus an unextractable alignment image of its relatives, so the example count from this paper is 1.
plain_idea.predict: Output would be a yes/no call on NAD+-rebuilding activity, with the true answer coming from mass-spectrometry product assays like the LC-MS assay used here. This paper provides that readout for two proteins (wild type and the Lys185Ala variant).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups studying how bacteriophages defeat bacterial immune systems would use a sequence-based screen to pick which of thousands of uncharacterised phage genes to test in the lab. But this paper cannot support it: the idea would need a pathway-wide survey, not one enzyme.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper. A single-enzyme structural mechanism study with three structures and roughly ten kinetic numbers has no feature/label table and no path to one. The broader topic (predicting phage anti-defence and NAD+-reconstitution functions from protein sequence) would need a pathway-scale survey such as a large phage genome collection with experimentally tested hits, not this paper.

effort.compute_note: Only the 3.18 MB supplementary bundle was actually downloaded and parsed; nothing was timed because no modelling task exists.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Query the RCSB data API for the three deposited PDB IDs and the EMDB API for the two map IDs. Took under a minute and killed it: all three structures return 404 and both maps are still on hold.

verdict_reason: Fails Part A1, A2, A3 and A5. The deposited structures and cryo-EM maps are all still embargoed (three PDB IDs return 404; both EMDB maps on hold), and even once released the entire dataset is three structures of one protein plus about ten kinetic values that exist only as pixels in figure panels. There is no table, no label column, and no sequence file. This is excellent mechanistic enzymology and a non-candidate for machine learning.
